newsitem.title: USA: Boeing offer boosts McDonnell debt.
newsitem.headline: Boeing offer boosts McDonnell debt.

text.p: Boeing Co's proposed $13 billion-plus buyout of McDonnell Douglas Corp propelled the price of the latter's outstanding debt, tightening spreads by 20 to 25 basis points, traders and analysts said.
The tentative stock-swap deal unveiled on Sunday would give McDonnell shareholders 0.65 share of Boeing stock for each McDonnell share currently owned.

Jim Drury, corporate bond analyst at Bear, Stearns & Co Inc, said Boeing's manageable proforma 28.1 percent debt to capital ratio would allow it to absorb the approximately $3.0 billion in outstanding McDonnell Douglas debt without negative implications to the company's bottom line.
"There's a lot of positives in this (merger)," Drury said. "They didn't pay a lot in terms of premium, they have a better balance, and the combined entity is substantially stronger."

Indeed, Moody's Investors Service placed the ratings of both companies on review for possible upgrade, based on the potential for improved cash flows, better economies of scale and the likelihood the combined entity would be a more successful bidder for new military programs.
Boeing's proforma outstanding debt, including that incurred by the purchase of aerospace and defense businesses of Rockwell International Corp ROK.N, totaled about $3.8 billion as of June 30, 1996.
The proforma combined debt to capital ratio would equate to 35 percent, Drury said.
McDonnell Douglas 6-7/8 percent debt of 2006 was quoted at 47 basis points spread bid, 42 offer on Monday compared with a 72 bid, 69 offer market on Friday.
Boeing debt also firmed but few trades were spotted. Boeing 8.10s of 2006 tightened two basis points to 41 bid, 38 offer near mid-session.

Drury noted McDonnell Douglas debt is still trading weaker than Boeing's, and further gains are possible. Commerce for both McDonnell Douglas and Boeing debt was thin at mid-session, according to traders.
The analyst also stressed the future of Boeing will be subject to how competitors Raytheon Co, Northrop Grumman Corp and Lockheed Martin Corp will respond.
McDonnell Douglas shares rose 9-3/4 points to 61-3/4 at mid-afternoon. Boeing shares were up more than 3-1/2 points.
